subject: DESIGN (item 2) creation-time pipeline misses: what is safe for CA, what to land first
body:
FACTS (C6p ui60 log)
- backboardd: 121 Mali entry=11 misses (9.7 s) and 35 AIR misses (all creation variant=4 ATTACHMENT_BLENDS, 4.6 s). SpringBoard: 8 Mali (1.4 s), 2 AIR.
- 349 pack hits and 136 memory hits cost almost nothing. So 'prewarm every pack-known pipeline at process start' would only move cheap deserialization. The cost is entirely in pipelines that are NOT in the pack/cache.

ORDER I PROPOSE
1) [DONE, in gates now] Disk cache survives builds.
   - tools/build_tegu_frontend_objects.sh now defaults NORD2_PIPELINE_CACHE_SCOPE=compilers.
   - The build id = both compiler archives + headers + cache/key sources (pipeline_cache.c, pipeline_cache_frontend.inc, library_frontend.inc). Every other compile input is already in each entry key, so a hit is byte-identical to a compile.
   - Effect: a frontend-only rebuild (render/encoder/executor) keeps the device disk cache and the pack valid. C6o's second boot of the same build went 13.8 s -> 3.5 s; that becomes the norm across builds.
   - Rollback: NORD2_PIPELINE_CACHE_SCOPE=all.
2) [root/corpus] Feed C6p's 166 TPC_MISS records (device misses.txt / TEGU_PSO_REC) into the next pack (build_pipeline_pack.py accumulation). Each first-use pipeline then becomes a pack hit on the next build.
3) [encode, next] Asynchronous creation, for what remains:
   - newRenderPipelineState returns at once with a 'building' pipeline. The build (AIR translate, generic prepare, default Mali compile, fallback chain) runs on 2 worker threads (user-initiated QoS; the little cores are at 1.8 GHz while the bigs sit at 0.73).
   - The first draw that needs it STEALS the build if it is still queued (builds inline: never worse than today) or WAITS if it is running.
   - Gain: the 59-miss episode creates its pipelines in bursts within one frame, so the compiles run 2-3 in parallel while CA keeps encoding. Est. -40..-60% of the 4 s worst episode. It does not help a single pipeline drawn right after creation.
   - CA SEMANTICS RISK: Metal returns nil plus an error synchronously. Under async, a later build failure can no longer be returned as nil: the draws would fail the command instead of CA skipping the layer.
   - SAFE RULE: go async only for descriptors whose AIR/Mali status was recorded as success (pack/corpus record or an earlier refusal-free record). Unknown descriptors stay synchronous. A background failure then marks the pipeline inert (drops its draws, logs TEGU_PIPELINE_ASYNC_FAILED), never failing the command.
4) [DONE, in gates] Draw-time variants: base stealing/waiting plus base-first worker order (details in the next STABLE post).

Unless you object, I start 3) after the item-1 stable point.
